Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: BCCL, OpenAI strike partnership to expand news discovery and publishing experience
Article Text:
BCCL content will be surfaced on ChatGPT with attribution and links to original stories.

Bennett, Coleman & Co Ltd (BCCL) and OpenAI have entered into a strategic partnership aimed to help readers discover journalism from BCCL’s publications through ChatGPT, while strengthening attribution and access to original reporting.Under the partnership, content from participating BCCL publications, including The Times of India and The Economic Times, will be surfaced in ChatGPT when relevant to user queries. Select summaries or excerpts will identify the publication and provide a direct link to the original article, allowing users to access the complete report and context on BCCL platforms.The partnership will cover live reporting and content from BCCL’s English and Indian-language publications.“For almost two centuries, BCCL has believed that journalism is a public trust - rooted in facts, guided by independent judgment, and sustained by the trust of our readers,” said Mohit Jain, chief operating officer and board member, BCCL. He said the partnership would enable audiences to discover journalism from across BCCL’s publications while preserving the “source, context, and identity of the original reporting.OpenAI vice-president, media partnerships, Varun Shetty said BCCL is an important part of how millions of people understand India and the world. “This partnership will help ChatGPT users discover reporting from BCCL’s English and Indian-language publications, with clear attribution and direct links to the original articles,” he said.The two companies will also explore applications of OpenAI technology across BCCL’s products, reader services and internal workflows. Areas under consideration include archive discovery, research, data analysis, translation, reader services and business operations.Any use of AI in BCCL newsrooms will remain subject to the editorial standards and policies of the respective publications, as well as human oversight.BCCL said its participating publications will retain complete editorial control over their journalism. Editors and journalists will continue to make decisions on reporting, verification, editing and publication, while OpenAI will have no role in determining their coverage or editorial positions.The partnership is part of OpenAI’s broader work with publishers globally to improve access to reliable information and explore AI applications across news products and publishing operations.
Article Summary: BCL content will be surfaced on ChatGPT with attribution and links to original stories. Select summaries or excerpts will identify the publication and provide a direct link to the original article, allowing users to access the complete report and context on BCCL platforms.

Article Title: Dire straits: Brand on the run as Trump suggests Hormuz can be renamed in his honor
Article Text:
Trump’s latest push to rename the Strait of Hormuz adds another chapter to his growing campaign of political branding and geographic renaming

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Donald Trump has rescued a canal, invaded a country, conquered a gulf, annexed a lake -- at least on American maps -- and put his name on a performing-arts center. He now appears to have set his sights on the hottest waterway on the planet.The MAGA boss suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” -- because if you cannot solve a problem, you can at least rename it.The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf of America for US federal purposes. Last week he signed an executive order changing Lake Ontario to Lake America, saying the US had been treated badly by Canada. He then helpfully suggested that the Atlantic or Pacific could be next, saying, “We have a gulf and we have a lake…Now all we need is an ocean. ”The President, someone jibed, appears to be collecting bodies of water like refrigerator magnets.The joke became even better when Google Maps and Apple Maps fell in line.Google changed Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users over the weekend. Apple followed on Tuesday. Canadians, however, continue to see Lake Ontario and users elsewhere may see both names. In other words, the lake has acquired the geographic equivalent of dual citizenship.The tech companies' compliance prompted criticism from illuminati who argue that private corporations should not allow political pressure to dictate historical and geographic nomenclature. MapQuest, an internet relic many Americans had forgotten existed, refused to make the change and suddenly discovered the most effective marketing strategy in Silicon Valley: stand up to Trump. Its downloads reportedly surged, giving it the kind reception normally reserved for rock bands that haven’t toured for a long time or sports legends making a comeback.There is also an awkward business joke buried underneath all this. Trump built his political persona partly on branding himself as a master businessman, but his corporate record includes repeated failures and bankruptcies in hotels and casinos; His casino empire alone went through multiple Chapter 11 restructurings. Trump-branded ventures have also included products and licensing deals that did not last.Late-night television has naturally treated Trump's naming obsession as premium material. The Atlantic, meanwhile, took the joke to its logical conclusion in a satirical vision of a future America in which everything is renamed “America” or “Trump,” leaving citizens unable to distinguish between brands of products, goods, and structures.Political analysts however see a serious calculation behind what many consider trolling. The renaming campaign sure is presidential theater -- cheap to stage, impossible for the internet and tv to resist, and almost guaranteed to ignite social media. But it also serves to distract people from more pressing issues -- such as cost of living and democracy going down the tubes.
Article Summary: Trump suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf Of America for US federal purposes.

Article Title: Dyson launches Airsmooth, its first dedicated hot air brush
Article Text:
Dyson Airsmooth uses two types of bristles

Dyson has launched the Airsmooth, its first dedicated hot air brush, aimed at making everyday hair styling easier while reducing the need for high heat. The device combines Dyson’s airflow technology with PivotFlex and Anti-snag bristle systems to dry, smooth and lift hair. Dyson says the Airsmooth is designed to work across straight, wavy, curly and coily hair types. The device is built for routines such as everyday smoothing, stretching curls and coils, and preparing hair for further styling. It also uses intelligent heat control that measures temperature 100 times a second while styling.The Dyson Airsmooth uses a patented dual-bristle system designed to guide hair through the device. The anti-snag bristles feature a looped structure that can collapse to release strands more easily. Dyson says this helps reduce snagging and breakage while improving comfort around the scalp.The second system is called PivotFlex. Its bristles have an open-base design that helps control and diffuse high-pressure airflow. They can flex by up to 90 degrees while the tapered shape helps hair wrap and release during styling.The two bristle systems are arranged in a teardrop formation to create tension from the roots to the ends.Dyson says the Airsmooth can be used on straight, wavy, curly and coily hair. The device is designed for drying and smoothing hair, stretching curls and coils, and creating a smoother base before another styling step. According to the company, the bristle system is designed to reduce tangles while helping control frizz.The Airsmooth also uses Dyson’s intelligent heat control technology, which measures temperature 100 times per second. The company says this system is designed to provide controlled heat during styling while helping protect the hair's natural texture.Dyson says the Airsmooth has a lightweight and ergonomic design for everyday use across different hair lengths. The device also supports universal voltage, allowing it to be used while travelling. Dyson positions it for use during routines such as getting ready for work, after a workout or while on holiday.The Dyson Airsmooth is introduced in select markets only. The launch in India will be announced closer to the availability.
Article Summary: The Dyson Airsmooth is designed to work across straight, wavy, curly and coily hair types. The device is built for routines such as smoothing, stretching curls and coils, and preparing hair for further styling. It also uses intelligent heat control that measures temperature 100 times a second while styling.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang congratulates OpenAI’s team on GPT-6 Astra launch, says ‘AGI has arrived’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia.

What changed under the hood

The Nvidia-OpenAI relationship

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has declared that artificial intelligence (AGI) has officially arrived, crediting OpenAI’s newly unveiled GPT-6 Astra model. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Huang congratulated ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and wrote, “GPT-6 Astra, trained on ~100K+ NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVLink72. From ChatGPT to o1 to Astra in 4 years. AGI has arrived. Congratulations @OpenAI team.” Huang further stated that GPT-6 Astra was trained on over 100,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72 systems, each designed to link 72 GPUs into a unified computing powerhouse. He initially cited 300,000 systems before revising the figure to 100,000. Looking ahead, Huang said 400,000 GPUs are coming online next, underscoring Nvidia’s central role in powering the AI revolution.The claim rests on a major shift in Nvidia's chip architecture. The company used to ship its processors eight to a board; its newer NVLink72 design instead wires 72 chips together to function as a single, unified system. That redesign came at enormous cost, and only pays off if a customer is training something large enough to need it. OpenAI's Astra model appears to be exactly that customer, according to Huang's figures.One detail has raised questions: Huang's original post reportedly cited 300,000 systems before he deleted it and reposted the smaller 100,000 figure, with no explanation offered for the discrepancy.The Nvidia-OpenAI relationship has also shown signs of cooling beneath the surface. A $100 billion deal the two companies announced in 2025 was reportedly never formally signed, and reporting in June indicated OpenAI had quietly scaled back its Nvidia chip purchases. Against that backdrop, markets are likely to pay closer attention to Huang's pledge of 400,000 additional GPUs coming online than to the AGI declaration itself — a claim that has already drawn skepticism online, with one social media user noting that reaching AGI by 2026 defies earlier expectations that it wouldn't happen until 2029 or later.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model trained on 100,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72 systems. He initially cited 300,000 systems before revising the figure to 100,00. Huang said 400,000 more GPUs are coming online next.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Mark Zuckerberg: “The biggest risk is not taking any risk…” - a reminder not to let fear make you miss an opportunity
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Mark Zuckerberg

“The biggest risk is not taking any risk... In a world that changing really quickly, the only strategy that is guaranteed to fail is not taking risks.”

Understanding the meaning behind today’s quote

Why inaction can become a risk

Mark Zuckerberg's early years at Facebook

The problem with waiting for certainty

What can be learned from the quote

Consider the risk of doing nothing: A decision to wait or stay with the familiar can have consequences of its own.

Define the risk clearly: Look at what could be lost, what could be gained and whether the decision can be reversed.

Start with smaller experiments: Testing an idea on a limited scale can reduce the potential cost of failure.

Do not confuse risk with recklessness: Taking a calculated risk involves understanding the possible outcomes rather than ignoring them.

Accept that certainty is rare: New ideas and opportunities rarely come with a guarantee of success.

Learn from unsuccessful decisions: A failed attempt can provide useful information for the next decision.

Keep changing circumstances in mind: A strategy that works today may become less effective as technology, markets or customer behaviour change.

Compare action with inaction: Instead of asking only what could go wrong by acting, consider what might happen if nothing changes.

A different way of looking at failure

The misconception about taking risks

Playing it safe can feel like the easiest way to avoid trouble. There is comfort in keeping a familiar job, sticking with a business model that already works or leaving an uncertain idea for another day. The difficulty is that circumstances do not always stay familiar. Industries change, technology moves on and opportunities can disappear while a decision is being postponed. Mark Zuckerberg's career has unfolded against that kind of uncertainty. From launching Facebook as a university student to making major bets on new technologies and online services, his work has involved decisions where the outcome could not have been known in advance.That does not mean every risk produces a good result, nor that caution is always a mistake. His observation is more specific than that. When the world is changing quickly, refusing to make uncertain choices can have consequences too. His well-known quote raises a simple question: what might standing still cost when everything around you is moving?Zuckerberg's point is fairly direct. When the environment around a person or organisation is changing quickly, avoiding every uncertain decision does not remove risk. It can create a different kind of risk, one that comes from remaining in a position that may no longer work.Consider a company with a product that has performed well for years. Keeping it unchanged may protect existing revenue and avoid the cost of developing something new. But if customers begin moving towards another type of product, the company can eventually find itself trying to respond after the market has already shifted.The same idea can apply to an individual. Staying in a familiar job avoids the uncertainty of changing careers. It also means accepting whatever happens to that existing role as the industry develops.The quote is therefore less about chasing danger and more about recognising that uncertainty exists whether or not someone chooses to act.Risk is often measured by asking what could go wrong after a decision is made. That is only half the calculation. There is also the question of what might happen if the decision is never made.A business that chooses not to develop a new technology may save money in the short term. If competitors invest successfully, however, the business may later need to spend considerably more just to catch up. The original decision looked conservative. Its longer-term consequences may be less so.For individuals, the same pattern can be harder to notice. Someone who never applies for a different position cannot be rejected from it. They also cannot get it. A person who decides not to learn a new skill avoids the effort involved, but may eventually find that the skill has become necessary.This does not make action automatically preferable. Sometimes the information available is too weak, the potential loss is too large or waiting genuinely is the better choice.Mark Zuckerberg was born in 1984 and attended Harvard University. While studying there, he developed a social networking website with fellow students. Facebook launched in 2004 and initially focused on university communities.The service expanded beyond Harvard and other universities relatively quickly. Zuckerberg eventually left Harvard to concentrate on the company as its user base grew.Facebook's early development took place during a period when internet use was changing quickly. Social networking was still a relatively new idea, and the company had to make decisions about expansion, advertising, technology and competition without knowing exactly how the market would develop.People often want enough information to know that a decision will work before making it. With genuinely new ideas, that point rarely arrives.A new product has no established sales record. A new technology may not yet have a settled market. A career change involves an unfamiliar environment. Waiting for certainty can therefore mean waiting until the uncertainty has already been resolved by someone else.Technology companies face this problem frequently. Products that seem unimportant at first can become widely adopted. Consumer habits can shift after the arrival of a new device or platform.Moving too early has its own disadvantages. A company can spend heavily on an idea before the market is ready. But waiting too long can produce a different problem, particularly when competitors have already gained experience.Failure is easier to notice than a missed opportunity. A failed business venture leaves behind bills and records. A rejected job application produces an email. A product that does not sell gives a company clear numbers to examine.The cost of doing nothing can be much quieter.There may be no obvious moment when a person realises that a skill should have been learned earlier. A business may never know exactly how much growth it lost because it delayed entering a market.This makes inaction psychologically easier to accept. Nothing visibly went wrong. Yet something can still have been lost.Zuckerberg's quote draws attention to this less visible side of decision-making. It does not make failure desirable. It simply suggests that avoiding failure completely is not the same as avoiding risk.The most obvious misunderstanding is that the quote means people should take as many risks as possible.Zuckerberg's statement specifically refers to a world that is changing quickly. The circumstances matter. A risk that makes sense for a technology company facing rapid disruption may make little sense for someone dealing with a completely different situation.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg was born in 1984 and attended Harvard University. While studying there he developed a social website with fellow students. Facebook launched in 2004 and initially focused on university communities. Zuckerberg eventually left Harvard to concentrate on the company as user base grew.

Article Title: Swiggy launches dedicated helpline and in-app channel for food safety complaints: Here’s how it will work
Article Text:
Swiggy launches dedicated customer support for food safety complaints

How to report a complaint

What happens after reporting

Swiggy has launched a dedicated 24x7 helpline and an in-app reporting channel for customers to raise food safety concerns related to their orders. The company said the new support options will allow customers to submit complaints directly and provide additional information or images related to an issue.Customers can call 7948231850 to register a food safety complaint with Swiggy's customer care team. The company has also added a ‘Food Safety’ channel under the Help section of its app for reporting such concerns.Customers have two options to report a food safety concern: the dedicated helpline or the new in-app channel. Here's how both options will work:Through the helpline: Customers can call 7948231850 and register their complaint with Swiggy's customer care team. After the call, they will receive a link on their registered mobile number to provide additional information and upload pictures related to the issue.Through the app: Customers can open the Help section and use the dedicated ‘Food Safety’ channel. They can describe the concern in a short message and upload relevant pictures. Swiggy said customers will receive a ticket number to track the status of their complaint.Complaints submitted through either channel will be reviewed by Swiggy's Food Safety Assurance Team, which the company said will review the issues on priority and take necessary action.Swiggy said the complaints will also help it identify repeated concerns and patterns across orders. The company plans to use this information to engage with restaurant partners and strengthen preventive measures related to food safety on the platform.Separately, Swiggy said it continues to work with its restaurant partners on food safety practices. This includes encouraging the use of quality ingredients, ensuring that menu descriptions accurately reflect ingredients, and periodically educating partners about hygiene practices and food safety standards.
Article Summary: Customers can call 7948231850 to register a food safety complaint with Swiggy's customer care team. The company has also added a ‘Food Safety’ channel under the Help section of its app for reporting such concerns.

Article Title: Huawei launches Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone in China, ahead of Apple’s September 9 event
Article Text:
Huawei Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone specifications and features

Huawei has launched the Mate XT 2, its third-generation trifold smartphone, in China. The timing of the release is notable as the phone makes its debut just two days before Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ event on September 9 where the company is expected to present its first-ever foldable iPhone.Huawei Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone price in ChinaThe flagship device will officially go on sale across China on September 10. Pricing begins at ¥19,999 (roughly $2,980) for an entry-level configuration featuring 16GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage. The top-tier variant, which packs 1TB of storage alongside an optional privacy screen, tops out at ¥24,999 (around $3,725).Departing from the outward folding mechanisms seen on earlier Mate XT iterations, Huawei redesigned the Mate XT 2 to fold inward along both sides of its 10.2-inch panel, taking cues from Samsung's Galaxy Z TriFold. The company also overhauled the hinge system to smooth out and soften the display crease along the bending lines.The top-spec Huawei Mate XT 2 becomes Huawei’s first foldable smartphone to offer a dedicated privacy screen feature. When activated, the viewing angles narrow significantly so that the panel looks nearly black from the side while staying clear to the person looking straight on. Huawei applies this privacy filter across the entire display at once, whereas Samsung’s tool can mask specific sections of the screen.When closed, the handset measures 12.3mm in thickness with 6.5-inch screen on top; when fully opened, the profile slims down to between 3.5mm and 4mm around the 10.2-inch workspace. Both screens feature LTPO AMOLED panels. The exterior cover screen supports refresh rates up to 120Hz at a resolution of 2,442 x 1,140 pixels. The expansive internal foldable display delivers a higher resolution of 3,184 x 2,232 pixels, running at a standard 90Hz, with only the top-tier version upgrading the inner panel to 120Hz.Under the hood is Huawei’s new Kirin 9050 Pro SoC, which the company states provides a 46% jump in performance compared to the prior Kirin 9030 Pro. The smartphone runs on a 5,600mAh battery supporting 66W wired USB-C fast charging and 50W wireless charging.The rear camera setup features a 50MP primary camera with a variable aperture ranging from f/1.49 to f/4.0, paired with a 40MP ultra-wide sensor and a 50MP periscope telephoto lens offering 3.5x optical zoom. Both the outer cover and main inner displays house an 8MP front camera.
Article Summary: Huawei has launched the Mate XT 2, its third-generation trifold smartphone, in China. Pricing begins at ¥19,999 (roughly $2,980) for an entry-level configuration featuring 16GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage. The top-tier variant, which packs 1TB of storage alongside an optional privacy screen, tops out at ¥24,000 (around $3,725)

Article Title: Tim Cook will not take stage during Apple iPhone 18 launch event
Article Text:
iPhone 18 launch event may not see Tim Cook taking stage

Tim Cook will watch the iPhone 18 launch from the audience

The transition has already begun behind the scenes

Tim Cook is still expected to have a role at Apple

For years, Tim Cook has been the familiar face of Apple ’s product launches, appearing on stage and in keynote videos as the company introduced new iPhones and other devices. That will change at the upcoming iPhone 18 event. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Cook will not appear in the pre-recorded Apple Event video, although he is expected to attend the screening at Apple Park as a VIP guest.The change comes as Apple completes its transition from Cook to John Ternus as CEO. Cook is moving into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board, while Ternus takes over as the company’s public-facing leader.Gurman wrote in his “Power On” newsletter that Cook will be present at the Apple Park screening with members of the press and other invited guests. His absence from the event video will allow Ternus to take the lead as Apple introduces its next generation of iPhones.The timing is also significant because the launch is expected to include Apple’s first foldable iPhone. Having Ternus lead the presentation gives the new CEO an opportunity to establish himself as Apple's face during an important product cycle.Cook’s move to chairman has involved changes beyond the stage.He has moved out of his previous office in Section 7 of Apple Park and is getting a new office, while Ternus has taken over the CEO office in the executive suite.The two executives have also praised each other during public appearances and in internal communications as the leadership change has progressed.Cook has made several public and internal farewells in recent months. He addressed the transition during his final earnings call, in a memo to employees and during the WWDC keynote.In his last CEO memo, Cook told employees that he looked forward to seeing them at Apple campuses around the world, making clear that he would remain involved with the company rather than leave it entirely.Although he will no longer present Apple's products, Cook is expected to remain active in his new role. His compensation also reflects the continuing nature of his role.As executive chairman, Cook will receive a base salary of $2 million and could receive up to $45 million in restricted stock units in 2027. By comparison, Art Levinson, the non-executive chairman whom Cook replaced, received less than $560,000 in salary, stock and other compensation last year.That means Cook's absence from the launch video should not be interpreted as an exit from Apple. He is expected to be at Apple Park for the event, watching the company's next chapter from a different place.The September launch will therefore mark a change in more than just the iPhone lineup. After years of seeing Cook introduce Apple's products, viewers will now see Ternus take that role while Cook watches from the audience.
Article Summary: Tim Cook will not appear in the pre-recorded Apple Event video, although he is expected to attend the screening at Apple Park as a VIP guest. The change comes as Apple completes its transition from Cook to John Ternus as CEO. Cook is moving into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board.

iOS 27 expected release date

iOS 27 features: New Siri and more AI tools

Users who joined Apple's beta programme could test the upcoming features before the final version.The final version is expected to be more stable than the beta builds and will be available as a regular software update for compatible iPhones.AI is one of the main areas of focus in iOS 27. Apple is introducing a more capable version of Siri that can understand natural language better and provide more useful assistance. The company is also adding AI-powered features to Photos, including tools for changing and editing images.Apple is also bringing Siri into the Camera experience. The feature can use what the camera is seeing to help users find information about objects and subjects in front of the iPhone.The update also includes new child safety features and wider improvements aimed at making iPhones more responsive.Apple says iOS 27 will work with compatible iPhones, with the update retaining broad device support. Current reports indicate support going back to the iPhone 11 and iPhone SE (2nd generation). However, not every iPhone will get access to every AI feature.
Article Summary: Apple is preparing to roll out iOS 27, the next major software update for iPhone users. The update was announced at WWDC 2026 and has already gone through developer and public beta testing. Apple is introducing a more capable version of Siri that can understand natural language better and provide more useful assistance. The company is adding AI-powered features to Photos, including tools for changing and editing images.
